definition: Circuitous means taking a long, indirect route rather than the direct one.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word circuitous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know circuitous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The ants took a circuitous trail around the whole counter, tripling the distance to the sugar bowl for no reason we could see.
A winding lane curves prettily and may still be the shortest way home; circuitous goes further, insisting the way runs far out of its way.
Labyrinthine outdoes circuitous: a circuitous route is long but gets you there by one traceable path, while a labyrinthine one tangles into so many turns you may be lost for good.

Roundabout is the everyday word for not going straight at a thing - a roundabout route, a roundabout apology. Circuitous means the same in more formal dress and suits official contexts: audits, itineraries, legal processes. If you would say it to a friend, use roundabout; in a report, circuitous.

Meandering means drifting lazily and aimlessly, curve by curve, like a slow river with nowhere to be. A circuitous route can be brisk and purposeful - it simply runs far out of its way. Meandering is about lacking an aim; circuitous is about the distance, not the mood.

Tortuous means full of twists and turns - it measures how tangled a path is, bend by bend. Circuitous measures something else: how far the way strays from direct. A mountain switchback is tortuous yet efficient; a detour looping around two counties is circuitous without one sharp turn.

The park sign lists the giant sequoia's circumference just under its age and height.
Circuitous means taking a long, indirect route rather than the direct one.
To get one lost library card reissued, Naomi collected a form from the registrar, a stamp from the bursar across campus, and a signature from an office open only every other Thursday.
The process was circuitous by design, she suspected - a paper journey that visited every building except the library.
Circuitous fits because the route - here a procedural one - runs far out of its way to reach a simple destination.
Winding wouldn't say that: a winding path can still be the shortest one.
Circuitous always means the long way around, whether on roads, in paperwork, or in an apology.
Circuitous describes routes and processes - real roads or paper-trail errands - that run the long way around.
It says nothing about hiding: a circuitous explanation eventually arrives at its point, where a cryptic one (this unit) hides the point on purpose.
For everyday talk, roundabout does the same job in plainer clothes.

The night of the marathon, the navigation app earned its bad reputation.
Our hotel stood eleven blocks from the arena — a straight shot down one avenue on any other night.
With the avenue closed, the app produced a circuitous alternative: north across the river, six miles along the far bank, and back over the second bridge.
My uncle fumed at every mile.
The route never twisted — long, straight boulevards the whole way — and traffic moved briskly.
What galled him was the arithmetic.
Eleven blocks had become nine miles.
We watched the arena's lights recede in the mirror before the second bridge finally swung us back toward them.
The app, to its credit, had promised exactly this: not a slow route, not a confusing one, only a long way around.
